thesis: Vertiv's ~19% 60-day decline traces to a confirmed, company-disclosed Q2 2026 earnings miss (reported July 29, 2026) attributed to execution delays in complex hyperscale data-center deployments, even though the same release raised full-year guidance and cited a roughly $15B order backlog. Multiple law firms have since announced investigations into the adequacy of Vertiv's prior disclosures, and whether the miss is a temporary timing issue (the bull case) or early evidence of demand/execution deterioration remains a genuinely unresolved question ahead of Q3 2026 results.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if Q3 2026 results show the delivery-timing issues reversing and backlog conversion reaccelerating toward prior guidance-implied rates, or if the securities-fraud investigations fail to produce any filed complaint.

thesis: Marvell's ~13% 60-day decline reflects a 'sell the news' reversal: shares ran up on an expanded Google custom-silicon deal, then fell after the Aug 27 Q2 FY2027 earnings beat and raised guidance because the print didn't clear a richly-valued bar, and the stock has a documented pattern of negative reactions even to beats. The picture stays mixed -- record revenue and raised FY2028 guidance sit against a freshly disclosed Google warrant that could dilute shares by roughly 6-7% as the deal scales.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if shares stabilize and break out above pre-earnings highs, if Q3 FY2027 results and guidance clearly break the pattern of 'beat but sell off,' or if buybacks are shown to offset the Google-warrant dilution faster than the market is pricing.

thesis: NVIDIA's ~11% 60-day rise is grounded in a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: fiscal Q2 FY2027 results (Aug 26, 2026) beat with $96.2B revenue (+106% YoY) and data-center revenue of ~$89B, and management raised Q3 guidance to $108B. The main live risk is 'circular financing' criticism of NVIDIA's investment/guarantee arrangements with AI-infrastructure partners (up to $105B in OpenAI-linked guarantees), which NVIDIA's own CFO has addressed directly rather than left unanswered, and no scheduled litigation ruling, dilutive raise, or leadership departure was found in the next ~90 days.
invalidation: Invalidated if hyperscaler/AI-infrastructure capex growth decelerates materially, if the financing arrangements with AI partners are shown to be masking weaker organic demand, if a material write-down occurs on NVIDIA's strategic investments, or if a near-term ruling emerges in the pending securities litigation.
sources: Bernstein Litowitz Berger & Grossmann LLP (securities litigation case page): https://www.blbglaw.com/cases-investigations/nvidia-corporation

thesis: AMD's ~16% 60-day decline traces mainly to a broad, sector-wide semiconductor selloff in July 2026 (AI-capex and circular-financing anxiety, a weak Samsung print) rather than any AMD-specific negative disclosure -- Q2 2026 results (Aug 4) actually beat with record $11.5B revenue (+50% YoY) and a strong Q3 guide (~$13B). Because the move is explained as macro/sector-wide rather than company-specific, this is scored low despite AMD's otherwise strong results and a clean risk profile this cycle.
invalidation: Invalidated if Q3 FY2026 earnings (expected early-to-mid November) miss the guided ~$13B revenue/margin trajectory, if the OpenAI/Meta GPU deployment milestones slip, or if the AI-capex macro overhang re-intensifies independent of AMD's own execution.
sources: Yahoo Finance (AMD Q2 2026 earnings call transcript): https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/earnings/AMD-Q2-2026-earnings_call-660937.html

thesis: Dell's ~11% 60-day rise follows a confirmed, company-disclosed $10B AI-infrastructure partnership with startup Volta (Aug 4, 2026) plus already-raised FY27 guidance from the May Q1 report, but Dell reports Q2 FY27 earnings today (Sept 1, 2026, after this run's data was pulled) -- an unresolved binary catalyst not yet tested. Dell also carries a disclosed governance history item: its FY2025 10-K (filed ~March 2025) reported a material weakness and a revision of prior-period financials tied to supplier-credit accounting errors.
invalidation: Invalidated if today's Q2 FY27 results or guidance miss the raised bar, if gross margins compress further on AI-server mix, or if the unremediated material weakness resurfaces with a new or larger misstatement.
sources: Dell Investor Relations (Q2 FY27 earnings date): https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/upcoming-events

thesis: SpaceX's ~12% 60-day decline reflects confirmed, company-disclosed developments -- Q2 2026 capex surged more than sixfold to $18.4B (mostly AI-related) alongside a $541M net loss, and a staggered post-IPO lockup began releasing hundreds of millions of shares from early August through a final unlock on Dec 8, 2026. A Morgan Stanley 'attractively valued' call (Aug 26) offers a counterweight, but it is an unresolved analyst opinion set against continued heavy cash burn and several more lockup tranches still ahead.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if the remaining lockup tranches pass without material net insider selling or price pressure, if Q3 2026 results show a credible narrowing of cash burn, or if the stock stabilizes well above IPO price with lockup-related pressure clearly abating.
sources: The Motley Fool (Q2 2026 earnings call transcript): https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/spacex-spcx-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

thesis: Intel's ~27% 60-day decline follows a confirmed, company-disclosed dilutive event -- an upsized $20B common stock offering priced Aug 10-18, 2026 -- layered on continuing Intel Foundry operating losses ($2.8B in Q2 2026 alone) even as Q2 revenue/EPS actually beat consensus. The picture remains mixed: a live, unresolved bull case (AI/data-center revenue +59% YoY, a reported Apple foundry customer win, $5B Nvidia and $2B SoftBank investments) sits against fresh dilution and a stock still trading below its own $95 offer price.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if Q3 2026 results (expected ~late October) show Foundry losses narrowing or a marquee external foundry customer commitment is confirmed, or if the stock reclaims and holds above the $95 offering price.

thesis: Sunbelt Rentals' ~7x volume spike on Aug 31-Sept 1 doesn't trace to any specific, confirmed company catalyst found in this cycle's research -- the closest dated events are a routine annual shareholder meeting and an ongoing buyback, neither of which plausibly explains a spike this size. The surrounding narrative remains an unresolved, pre-existing analyst debate over margin pressure since June 2026 earnings, with Q1 FY2027 results due Sept 9, 2026 as the next real test.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if Q1 FY2027 results (Sept 9, 2026) show margin stabilization, if a specific positive catalyst is confirmed for the volume spike, or if the pending construction-equipment-rental antitrust MDL is dismissed with prejudice as to Sunbelt.
sources: Berger Montague (construction equipment rental antitrust MDL): https://bergermontague.com/construction/
U.S. Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation (MDL No. 3152 docket report): https://www.jpml.uscourts.gov/sites/jpml/files/Pending_MDL_Dockets_By_District-July-1-2026.pdf

thesis: Avery Dennison's ~6.5x volume spike on Aug 31, 2026 coincided with a market-wide risk-off session (renewed U.S.-Iran tensions, an oil-price spike) and only a ~2% price decline, with no AVY-specific news found to explain either the spike or a preceding two-week drift lower. Q2 2026 results (July 30) actually beat and full-year guidance was raised, but management flagged an unresolved ~$0.50 sequential EPS headwind for Q3 from customer inventory unwind and raw-material inflation.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if a company-specific, confirmed catalyst emerges tied to renewed volume/price strength, or if Q3 2026 results clear the flagged margin headwind without new adverse disclosures.
